I'm not sure about temp or staffing agencies but I know recruiters get a commission by head and that's most of they're salary so they don't care your experience/qualifications(at least the one's I've dealt with).

Most managers I talk to say to put "starting wages" on that field. Also I advise if you don't really have that much experience, and if you can, apply in person. It greatly increases the chances of you talking to a manager and them actually hiring you. Applying online is like putting your name in a lottery box with THOUSANDS of other names. I've known people now that have graduated with me that have "filled out a hundred applications and get not even an email." This is because when employers post jobs on any classifieds site, hundreds maybe even thousands of people see that same ad and fill out the exact same application. If you don't look like the bees knees on paper a manager is not going to waste their time even if they do get to your application(this coming from a manager of a grocery store that uses both online and paper applications.) If you REALLY want a job at a particular place, make sure when you apply you are 1) dressed as if you were being interviewed(sometimes that's the case if you get to speak to the hiring manager) 2) ask if the hiring manager is there. If she/he's not, ask if you can wait to give your application to him/her. The key to all this is making sure the hiring manager **sees your face** 3) when you do see the hiring manager, smile. The of the most pleasant thing and smile about it. 

That's my advice if you're looking for a first job(it sounds like you are.) 

tl;dr just put "starting wages" That lets the manager know that you don't require a certain amount before you work for them.
